svg.aria-label: Workflow: the steps from the building profile to the validated semantic data model, the two data routes, how each step uses the inputs, where the agent, the tools and the batch runner work, and where you confirm or decide
svg.text: Goes back to an earlier step
Claude Code with the skills, in your session
claude -p on each image, without you

g.text: Timeseries route
BACnet route
the routes join
same tools from here; BACnet extras as noted
One-time setup: the Brick indexes, shared by all buildings
no skill
BRICK
Brick_nightly.ttl: the development version of Brick 1.5.0, with REC, provided in the
repository. The steps use the two indexes made from it, not this file.
TOOL
build-brick-classification-index.ts writes the class index: each class with its Brick
tags, read by the tools. build-brick-relationship-index.ts writes the relationship
index, read by the agent through the skills. Both indexes are provided; run the two tools
again when you use a newer Brick version.
Inventory: the building profile
point-mapping skill
AGENT
Lists your files and proposes the route: a point list and objects.json give timeseries;
devices.csv and object files give BACnet. Then drafts the profile with you.
TAGS
Header and sample rows → delimiter,
columns, the marker for an empty cell, and rows
to skip.
TAGS
Tags sorted by their pattern → how a
tag splits into its zone or plant and its point
abbreviation.
SQL IDS
Listed as the source of the ids and
units.
TAGS
devices.csv columns → the device
roles.
TAGS
Object names sorted by their pattern →
rules that clean the names, place each object
in a plant or zone, skip some, merge copies,
and split each name into parts.
SQL IDS
None: the object names are the ids.
BMS
Opens a few images of each kind and drafts the screen guide, the notes, and which screens
show which plant serves which zone.
BIM
Installation IFC: its system names compared with the plant list → the rule that matches
each system name to a plant.
DOCS
Listed in the profile: legends, function descriptions, a zone matrix.
TOOL
write-building-profile.ts checks the profile against your data and writes
building-config.json. Timeseries: row counts, skipped rows and empty cells. BACnet:
counts per rule, example splits, objects on several controllers and objects no rule places.
You confirm
Route, the input list and the
plant-abbreviation pattern.
Timeseries: the point-list format
(delimiter, columns, empty-cell marker,
rows to skip) and the naming rules, with
the number of tags each pattern sorts as
zone or plant.
BACnet, one decision at a time: device
roles, name cleanup, each placement rule
with example names split by it, each
skip rule, each object on several
controllers, and the name patterns no
rule places (they become points of their
controller).
Screen guide, notes, which screens show
which plant serves which zone, and the
rule for IFC system names, before image
analysis starts.
Point dictionary
before point mapping · point-mapping skill
AGENT
Drafts each entry: meaning, Brick tags and source. Writes only through
write-point-dictionary-entry.ts.
TAGS
Every point abbreviation, suffix and plant abbreviation gets an entry. Every frequent
description word gets an entry or is recorded as ignored. Each point's description is
checked against the meaning the documents give. BACnet: also the state names (On, Off, Auto
…), and unit spellings outside the standard BACnet unit names.
SQL IDS
Timeseries: each unit symbol (°C, m³/h) gets an entry.
DOCS
Legends and function descriptions: each meaning is quoted word for word, with file and
place (search-supporting-docs.ts). Legend rows that are not in your data are recorded,
not entered.
BRICK
Every Brick tag in an entry must exist in the class index.
TOOL
review-dictionary-draft.ts lists what is still open.
write-point-dictionary-entry.ts promote writes point-dictionary.json when nothing is
open.
You confirm or change
One at a time, with the evidence:
documents that contradict the data,
entries changed from before, new and
flagged entries, entries with no source,
entries carried over with no fresh
evidence, two words in one description
that give different kinds of point, and
legend rows, removed entries and ignored
words not yet recorded.
One table: entries with only the data as
source, no document.
A count: entries where documents and
data agree.
Open lists: frequent words with no
entry, and points where nothing says
what kind of point it is (sensor,
setpoint, command …) or what it
measures.
Later: gaps from later steps come back
here the same way.
Parse inputs
no skill
TAGS
The point list is split into plant
rows and zone rows.
TAGS
No split: the device list and the
object files are read as they are.
BIM
Every storey and space of the architecture IFC, and room → plant from the installation
IFCs.
TOOL
split-pointlist-csv.ts splits the point list (timeseries). build-spatial-hierarchy.py
reads the IFC files.
Point mapping
point-mapping skill
AGENT
Runs the mapper. Takes abbreviations and suffixes with no entry, frequent words with no
entry, words that give different kinds of point, and points with no kind or quantity back
to the dictionary review. Then runs the mapper again, keeping the points you reviewed, and
classify-all.ts.
TAGS
Each row becomes a point of its plant
or zone (map-plant-points.ts,
map-zone-points.ts).
SQL IDS
Joined by point id to the
objects.json names: id, object type and unit.
Meter readings with no point-list row are added
from objects.json.
TAGS
Each object is placed in a plant or
zone by the profile's rules
(map-bacnet-points.ts). Skip rules drop some,
merge rules join copies. Objects no rule places
become points of their controller itself.
SQL IDS
The object name is the id; type, unit
and state names come from the object file.
TOOL
map-points.ts runs the route's mapper. The dictionary gives each point the meaning of its
abbreviation and suffix.
Equipment from the tags
equipment-inventory skill
TOOL
update-equipment.ts --bms makes one item per device whose abbreviation the dictionary
names as equipment (a fan, a valve …). Extra points of the same device, such as an alarm
suffix, add no item. The item id is the point abbreviation (timeseries) or abbreviation and
number (BACnet).
Zone-to-room links
point-mapping skill
AGENT
Drafts the rule from zone ids to room numbers and reads the sources into rows. Writes the
rule, the rows, the check flags and your decisions with write-zone-rooms.ts.
BMS
Room overviews: floor, name, room number and use. Room-schematic headers: zone id and name.
One image at a time, saved after each.
BIM
Room numbers and names, storeys and space types (from step 1). Their names become
dictionary words: room types, and storeys and spaces to leave out.
DOCS
Zone matrix rows: zone, room, floor and name.
TOOL
match-zone-rooms.ts checks each zone against the sources, lists what needs you
(--review), then writes the floors, rooms and zones. After step 3 it runs again and also
checks that the zone's plant serves the room.
You confirm and decide
The rule from zone ids to room numbers,
with its hit rate and misses, and each
check's two computed flags: does it
count, is it independent. You can
override a flag, with a reason.
Each listed zone, one at a time: a check
disagrees, or no IFC room fits. Accept
the proposed room, pick another IFC
room, create one from the documents, or
leave it unlinked, with a reason.
Rule-only zones: no check fails, but
none confirms the room on its own. One
decision for the group.
Stale decisions: a rule, source or
dictionary change altered what an answer
was based on. The zone is listed again,
never relinked silently.
Connections
building-connections skill
AGENT
Reads one image at a time and saves after each (update-connections.ts). For each zone
whose plant only one source shows, re-reads the screenshot, decides, and tells you what it
decided.
BMS
Plant overviews and plant schematics: which plant serves which plant, and which plants are
part of another plant.
BMS
Floorplan colours or the room schematic's plant button, as the profile says: which plant
serves which zone.
BIM
Installation IFC systems: which plant serves which room, and through the zone-to-room links
which zone.
TOOL
reconcile-feeds-ifc.py compares, per plant, the zones it serves in the IFC with the zones
it serves in the screenshots.
Equipment from the screenshots
equipment-inventory skill
AGENT
One image at a time, saved after each (update-equipment.ts). On each plant it first
proposes the positions in the duct or pipe (supply, return …) and each medium (hot water,
chilled water …), with its reasons, and writes them only after you confirm. Then it reruns
the dictionary review with the image positions. A dictionary entry that tags all its points
as one stream (supply, return …), while the images put them on different streams, goes back
to the review.
BMS
Plant schematics: the plant's title, type, controller and station; each piece of equipment,
its position in the duct or pipe and its medium.
BMS
Room schematics: the zone's dampers, valves and sensors, and the fields at the top of the
screen.
BATCH
Optional: run-equipment-extraction.ts runs claude -p on each image without you. It
writes equipment without positions or medium, and skips plants whose positions are already
confirmed. Your confirmations follow in your session.
TOOL
validate-ductpath.ts checks each air position against the supply or extract marker in the
equipment's name. audit-classes.ts checks each medium against the equipment's class.
You confirm or correct

text.tspan: Per plant, before anything is written:

g.text: the positions in the duct or pipe and
each medium.
Air: intake, supply, return, exhaust
(and preheat), read from the
heat-recovery unit.
Water: read from the exchanger or meter,
else the loop's pump and valve or mixing
shunt. Supply and return on a plain or
mixing loop; an exchanger's primary and
secondary sides; a hot-water tank's coil
is primary; supply, circulation return
and make-up on the domestic hot-water
side.
Medium of each pump, tank, valve, coil
and exchanger: hot, chilled, domestic,
cold or condenser.
Also: the link between a screen label
and its point-list id, and each medium
the audit finds contradicting the
equipment's class.
Classification
brick-assign skill
AGENT
For each group of review points with the same flags and the same deciding dictionary
entries, proposes one verdict. Writes it with assign-brick.ts, or fixes the dictionary
entry behind it through the dictionary review. After a dictionary change:
compare-classes-by-cause.ts groups the class changes, apply-class-verdicts.ts applies
your verdicts.
TAGS
Through the dictionary: the point abbreviation and suffix of each tag and the description
words (BACnet: also state names), from step 2.
SQL IDS
The unit gives what is measured. The object type only checks that on/off points and
measured values get matching classes.
BMS
From step 4: each item's confirmed position and medium, and the plant's title and
equipment, which check the plant class. From step 3: which plant serves which, so a plant
with no water type of its own (hot, chilled, domestic) takes it from the plant that serves
it.
BIM
Room and storey names, through dictionary words, give the room and floor classes.
BRICK
The class index: the class whose Brick tags best match the point's tags.
TOOL
classify-all.ts decides, for each point, what kind of point it is (sensor, setpoint,
command …), what it measures, the medium and the flow, and classifies points, plants,
equipment, zones, floors and rooms. group-low-confidence.ts groups the points to review.
You review
Each review group: points flagged for
review, with low confidence, or where
another class would keep something this
one drops, grouped by their flags and
the dictionary entries that decided
them. The agent finds the cause and
proposes a verdict: keep the class, a
more specific class, a dictionary fix,
or ambiguous. You confirm or correct it,
a few groups per round.
After a dictionary change: the class
changes, grouped by old class, new class
and the entry that decided them. You
judge each group better or worse.
Reviewed points in a better group take
the new class; a worse group goes back
to the dictionary.
Generate data model
generate-ttl skill
TAGS
BACnet: devices.csv gives the devices, and each device is checked against it.
SQL IDS
Each point's database id becomes its link to its time series, and each link is checked
against the ids from step 2.
BRICK
The class index: the classes in the model, each checked to exist and not be deprecated.
TOOL
generate-ttl.ts writes outputs/building.ttl from the files of steps 2 to 5.
validate-ttl.ts checks Turtle syntax, classes, relations and references.
validate-refs.ts checks the time-series links and, on BACnet, the devices.
back to the dictionary review
runs again
Query
building.ttl
directly with SPARQL, or import it into a database
such as GraphDB for scalable storage and reasoning.
